reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified code at data_column_verification.rs:688, blob_verification.rs:536, and block_verification.rs:991 - all three gossip paths call get_beacon_proposer_indices (plural) which recomputes from active validators. However, this is NOT a spec violation. The 01e property (outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W0B1_1771748647.json, lines 561-577) requires get_beacon_proposer_index (singular) to use proposer_lookahead cache, which it correctly does (beacon_state.rs:1144-1153). The plural function is a separate helper that computes all proposers for an epoch - it's not governed by the same spec requirement. All gossip paths use the same recomputation method, so all nodes reach consensus. The claimed divergence scenario relies on proposer_lookahead becoming stale during partial_state_advance, but this cannot happen: partial_state_advance calls per_epoch_processing when crossing epoch boundaries (per_slot_processing.rs:42-48), which updates proposer_lookahead (single_pass.rs:469). Both cache and recomputation use deterministic computation from the same state, so results must match. No consensus split is possible. This is a design choice (optimization vs spec literal interpretation), not a vulnerability.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e invariant PROP-56ad1eb2-inv-018: 'get_beacon_proposer_index must return proposer_lookahead[slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH], not recompute' - applies to singular function only, which is correctly implemented.
